_comment: Packages the Lambda-provided payload must contain that no aws-sdk-js-v3 checkout can produce.
awsSdkShims: deprecated pre-Smithy-migration re-export shims. Each one's dist-cjs is a single
__exportStar of its @smithy counterpart. They were removed from this repo during that migration
and exist only as published npm artifacts, frozen at the versions below. Every name here has
shipped in the payload before, so customer functions may still require() it; dropping any is a
customer-breaking change.
smithyTwins: the @smithy packages those shims re-export, which the SDK no longer depends on
directly, or depends on only indirectly, so a dependency walk does not reach them. These MUST
be pinned explicitly rather than left to npm. The shims declare 2023-era ranges — for instance
@aws-sdk/util-middleware@3.374.0 asks for @smithy/util-middleware@^1.0.1 — so installing them
alone resolves 1.x, while the payload runs them against 4.x. Nothing nests under a shim, so each
re-export resolves up to the hoisted modern version, and the recorded API surface was captured
against those. Resolving to 1.x drops exports that surface requires (getSmithyContext,
ChecksumStream, headStream and ~30 more).
Three twins are pinned at 2.x while the rest are 4.x (is-array-buffer, util-buffer-from,
util-utf8). That is deliberate and measured: those are the versions the payload ships today.
overrides: three packages whose published dist-cjs re-exports a package that lacks exports the
payload's recorded API surface includes. The build this replaces applied the same redirects. It
is a content redirect, not a version pin — no published version of the declared dependency has
the missing exports. Every target must also appear in the lists above, or the redirect points at
a package that is not in the tree.
Installing these does not conflict with assembling from the local workspace, which exists
because the version being released is not on the registry at build time. All of these are
long-published and immutable.
